title: Minsap alerts about the circulation of chikungunya in Cuba and highlights territories with higher incidence - CiberCuba

analysis.time: Minsap confirmed the circulation of chikungunya in Cuba on September 28, 2026. The previous epidemic in 2025 had a significant impact, with over 20,000 cases reported by early November 2025. The current situation involves areas with high incidence rates, and the analysis was released in September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The Ministry of Public Health of Cuba (Minsap) highlighted Pinar del Río, Sancti Spíritus, Villa Clara, and several municipalities in Havana as areas with higher incidence rates. The warning was specifically directed at pregnant women in the last trimester, newborns, young children, and individuals with chronic illnesses such as heart disease and diabetes.
analysis.event: Minsap confirmed the circulation of chikungunya in Cuba and identified areas with higher incidence rates. The Deputy Minister of Public Health, Carilda Peña García, stated that the disease is circulating and emphasized the need for vigilance, especially among vulnerable groups.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The 2025 epidemic affected virtually the entire country, with over 20,000 cases reported. The current areas with high incidence rates have a larger number of susceptible individuals due to fewer infections during the previous outbreak. The disease can lead to prolonged joint pain and inflammation, and there is a risk of transmission to newborns if mothers contract it near delivery.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Minsap is maintaining surveillance over dengue and other diseases, and the response includes clinical differentiation from dengue, prevention measures such as eliminating breeding sites, and protecting water storage tanks. The official also acknowledged challenges in water, sanitation, and mosquito control due to limited fuel availability.

analysis.brief_en: The Ministry of Public Health of Cuba (Minsap) confirmed the ongoing circulation of chikungunya in the country as of September 28, 2026. The disease is currently prevalent in Pinar del Río, Sancti Spíritus, Villa Clara, and several Havana municipalities. These areas have a higher incidence rate, likely due to fewer infections during the severe 2025 epidemic, which saw over 20,000 cases by early November. The Deputy Minister of Public Health, Carilda Peña García, warned about the prolonged joint pain and inflammation associated with chikungunya, emphasizing the risk for pregnant women near delivery, newborns, young children, and individuals with chronic conditions like diabetes and heart disease. Minsap is focusing on differentiating chikungunya from dengue, implementing prevention measures such as eliminating breeding sites and protecting water storage, and addressing challenges in water and sanitation due to limited fuel for fumigation. The situation remains under active monitoring, with a complicated hygiene scenario in high-incidence areas.

title: Genomic study tracks massive chikungunya epidemic on Réunion Island

analysis.location_and_population: Réunion Island, with more than 54,000 confirmed cases and 43 deaths, affecting a significant portion of the population.
analysis.event: A massive chikungunya epidemic occurred on Réunion Island, with the virus spreading to other Indian Ocean islands and temperate regions of Europe and China.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: More than 54,000 confirmed cases and 43 deaths were reported. The estimated population immunity reached 66%, leading to a low risk of large resurgence.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Genomic surveillance and phylodynamic analyses were conducted to track the virus's evolution, spread, and eventual decline. The study concluded that the epidemic likely stemmed from a single introduction and that population immunity was a key factor in its decline.

analysis.brief_en: A genomic study has revealed the dynamics of a massive chikungunya epidemic on Réunion Island between August 2024 and June 2025, which saw over 54,000 confirmed cases and 43 deaths. The virus spread to other Indian Ocean islands and even reached temperate regions of Europe and China. Researchers from Belgium, France, and the United States used phylodynamic and phylogeographic methods to analyze the outbreak, indicating that it likely originated from a single introduction and spread through frequent human movements. The epidemic's decline was attributed to climatic conditions and the gradual build-up of population immunity, with an estimated 66% of the population now immune. This immunity, in theory, was sufficient to bring the effective reproduction number below 1, ending the outbreak. The study highlights the importance of integrating genomic, demographic, environmental, and immunity data for better epidemiological assessment and future preparedness.

title: CHP Warns Public About Dengue and Chikungunya Risks During Mid-Autumn Festival Celebrations

analysis.location_and_population: The CHP also reminded members of the public to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites when engaging in outdoor activities during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, such as visiting parks, grassy areas and beaches, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases.
analysis.event: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health warned the public about the risks of dengue fever and chikungunya fever during the Mid-Autumn Festival celebrations. No new chikungunya cases were reported, but one imported dengue case was recorded.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 32 dengue cases recorded in Hong Kong so far this year, including 30 imported cases and 2 local cases. 82 chikungunya cases were recorded last year, including 11 local cases. The global incidence of dengue has increased over the past two decades, with over 14 million cases reported in 2024.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CHP reminded the public to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and maintain good environmental hygiene. The situation is under investigation, and further assessments are ongoing.

analysis.brief_en: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of Hong Kong warned the public about the risks of dengue fever and chikungunya fever during the Mid-Autumn Festival celebrations. One imported dengue case was recorded, while no new chikungunya cases were reported. Hong Kong has recorded 32 dengue cases so far this year, including 30 imported cases and 2 local cases. The global incidence of dengue has increased over the past two decades, with over 14 million cases reported in 2024. The CHP advised the public to take preventive measures, including using insect repellents and maintaining good environmental hygiene.
